title: Chronal credit trading preemptor with adaptive KV compaction
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Introduce a new preemption policy (Chronal Credit Trading Preemptor) that assigns time-slice credits to inflight requests based on SLO slack and tenant weight, and allows soft-trading of credits between slices. Integrate this with an adaptive KV compaction/eviction component that considers expected reuse probability to reduce GPU memory pressure while preserving hot KV residency. The goal is to improve 95/99p latency SLOs under memory pressure and to provide a smoother fairness curve across tenants while limiting destructive KV churn.
background: We currently use slice-based preemption tuned by static priorities and per-tenant weights. Under sustained multi-tenant pressure, aggressive preemption causes high KV eviction churn and tail latency spikes. Previous tickets explored SLO-aware batching and token-budget schedulers, but we still see cases where reclaiming memory for a high-priority burst causes large eviction storms and subsequent degradation for other tenants. This design explores a credit-trading model coupled with conservative KV compaction to balance responsiveness and long-term KV hit-rate.
goals: Reduce 99p generation tail latency during mixed workloads by >= 15% on benchmark traces
Limit cold KV eviction spike magnitude (evictions/sec) when preemption occurs
Provide per-tenant controllable SLO-to-credit mapping so customers can express latency vs cost trade-offs
Maintain overall GPU memory headroom > 4% under normal load to avoid OOMs
non_goals: Replace existing batch admission controls — this augments, not supersedes, admission logic
Implement hard real-time guarantees; policy is probabilistic and best-effort
Porting to on-prem packaging in this PR — keep to hosted and Dedicated flows
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiments on internal 8-GPU and 64-GPU clusters show >=15% 99p reduction vs baseline traces
KV hit-rate drops by < 5% vs baseline under equivalent load, eviction churn reduced by >= 30%
No increase in 5xx customer-visible errors attributable to preemption logic in canary window
Feature gates and runtime flags exist: chronal_credit_enabled, kv_adaptive_compaction_threshold
design_decisions: Credit model: each inflight request is given a time credit budget measured in ms-of-execution (chronal credits). Credits are a function of tenant SLO slack, tenant weight, and recent SLA misses (adaptive replenishment).
Trading: short-running slices can donate unused credits to a shared pool for the allocation epoch (100ms) — enables bursts without hard-priority starvation.
Preemption policy: when scheduler needs to reclaim GPU time, it orders candidates by (credit deficit, predicted KV recovery cost, EMA of recent service) and preempts the smallest-impact slices first.

KV cost model: expected reuse probability estimated from per-key recency and model-specific heuristics (prefix reuse, prompt similarity). Eviction cost = estimated recompute tokens + network cost if remote checkpointing needed.
Adaptive compaction: instead of immediate eviction, mark low-reuse KV entries for compaction (quantize/pack) when memory pressure crosses soft threshold; full eviction reserved for hard threshold.
tradeoffs: Complexity vs predictability: credit trading adds bookkeeping and slightly higher scheduling CPU overhead but reduces destructive eviction cycles.
Approximate cost modeling: the KV reuse predictor is heuristic and may misclassify hot keys; we bias toward under-evicting to avoid regressions for critical tenants.
Latency vs memory: compaction preserves logical entries but increases per-access decode cost; we enable it only under pressure windows.
Fairness smoothing: EMA-based smoothing resists transient spikes but delays full corrective rebalancing for pathological tenants
implementation_plan: 1) Implement chronal credit bookkeeping in scheduler core (C++): credit assignment, epoch accounting, donation pool
2) Add preemption comparator that integrates credit deficit and KV eviction cost API
3) Expose runtime flags and per-tenant mappings via control plane (API + Console hooks)
4) Implement KV compaction path: mark-for-compaction, compaction worker, and compacted-entry accessor path
5) End-to-end e2e test harness and synthetic workloads to reproduce high-churn scenarios
6) Canary rollout: start on a small Dedicated fleet, monitor metrics, then widen to hosted pool if stable
test_plan: Unit tests for credit arithmetic, donation accounting and failure modes
Property tests: invariants (credit conservation within epoch, no negative credits)
Integration tests: scheduling under artificial pressure traces (multi-tenant replay) comparing baseline and new policy
KV correctness tests for compacted entries (lossless logical semantics)
Load tests: 8-GPU and 64-GPU replay of production telemetry that previously triggered eviction storms
Canary validations: 72-hour canary in dedicated pool with strict rollback criteria
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind chronal_credit_enabled; default off for 1 day after merge
Stage 1: internal QA cluster runs for 48 hours
Stage 2: alpha Dedicated pool (5 customers) for 72 hours
Stage 3: widen to low-traffic hosted region for 7 days
Rollback conditions: >3% increase in customer 5xx or >10% drop in KV hit-rate sustained for 30m
monitoring_dashboards: new dashboard runtime -> schedulers -> chronal-credit with panels for credits distribution, preemption candidates, kv cost heatmap
